name: Autosomal Dominant Intermediate Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type E

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Electrophysiological Diagnostic Criteria for CMT

criteria.description: Presence of autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
Nerve conduction studies showing intermediate conduction velocities (25-45 m/s)
Distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly affecting lower limbs with sensory loss
Identification of pathogenic variants in the DNM2 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of autosomal dominant family history, characteristic clinical features, and intermediate nerve conduction velocities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and electrophysiological criteria are met.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal muscle weakness and atrophy of lower limbs
Intermediate nerve conduction velocity slowing (25-45 m/s)
pathognomonic.notes: Electrophysiological hallmark distinguishing intermediate CMT from demyelinating or axonal forms

common.symptomName: Distal sensory loss in feet and hands
searchTerms: reduced sensation in fingers and toes

common.symptomName: Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes

occasional.symptomName: Mild distal sensory neuropathy in upper limbs
searchTerms: early sensory loss in upper limbs
slight sensory nerve damage in arms
difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness

imaging: MRI may show muscle atrophy in distal limbs
Spinal imaging to assess for scoliosis if clinically indicated
genetic: Pathogenic variants in DNM2 gene associated with autosomal dominant intermediate CMT type E
other: Electrophysiological studies demonstrating intermediate slowing of nerve conduction velocities

distinguishingFeatures: Axonal neuropathy with normal or mildly reduced conduction velocities (>45 m/s)
Predominant axonal degeneration on nerve biopsy

redFlags: Rapidly progressive weakness or sensory loss
references: Rossor AM, Polke JM, Houlden H, Reilly MM. Clinical implications of genetic advances in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Nat Rev Neurol. 2013;9(10):562-571.
Orphanet: Autosomal dominant intermediate Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type E. ORPHA:93114.
